GPTR-F-002-S67.title: Token Schema and Storage Contract
GPTR-F-002-S67.description: Define and implement the token persistence schema including fields for token_id, hashed_token, issued_at, expires_at, revoked_at, parent_token_id (for rotation chains), scopes, and actor metadata. Ensure compatibility with existing MongoDB patterns and GPTReader access constraints.
GPTR-F-002-S67.evidence: Code/DataPipelines/gpt_reader.py; Code/Shared/brain_auth.py; Code/Shared/ChatHealthyMongoUtilities.py; GAP: No formal token lifecycle schema currently defined

GPTR-F-002-S68.title: Token Expiration Enforcement Logic
GPTR-F-002-S68.description: Implement expiration validation in the authentication flow ensuring tokens past expires_at are rejected. Include optional lazy cleanup or TTL index alignment to prevent use of expired tokens without requiring immediate deletion.
GPTR-F-002-S68.evidence: Code/DataPipelines/auth.py; Code/DataPipelines/gpt_reader.py; GAP: Expiration not enforced beyond basic validation

GPTR-F-002-S69.title: Token Rotation Chain Logic
GPTR-F-002-S69.description: Implement secure token rotation logic that issues a new token, links it to the prior token via parent_token_id, invalidates or deprecates the old token based on policy, and ensures only the latest active token in a chain is valid.
GPTR-F-002-S69.evidence: Code/DataPipelines/auth.py; GAP: No rotation chaining or parent-child token tracking exists

GPTR-F-002-S70.title: Auth Middleware Integration with Lifecycle Checks
GPTR-F-002-S70.description: Integrate token lifecycle validation (expiration, revocation, rotation status) into the existing bearer token authentication flow used by GPTReader and Azure Functions, ensuring all requests enforce the full lifecycle policy consistently.
